features.method: OpenStreetMap way 162058026 (building=yes, name SLAC Klystron Gallery); nodes kept verbatim from an Overpass extract, no simplification. The Klystron Gallery is the continuous above-ground structure built directly over the buried linac beam tunnel it powers (per Wikipedia's Linear particle accelerator article, the gallery stretches above the path of the accelerator tunnel); its own footprint is used here as the accelerator's surface trace, honestly represented as a building feature rather than the buried tunnel itself.
features.name: SLAC linear accelerator (Klystron Gallery structure)

features.method: Nine OpenStreetMap building=yes ways from the same Overpass extract, drawn as context (no atlas entity/experiment is recorded at any of them): PEP Interaction Region 4 (bldg 640), PEP Interaction Region 6 (bldg 660), PEP Interaction Region 8 (bldg 680), PEP Interaction Region 12 (bldg 720), PEP Control Room (bldg 685), PEP Beam Facility/SSRL x2 (bldg 650, 730), End Station A (bldg 61), End Station B (bldg 62). Building numbers cross-checked against the official SLAC Area Map (src:geo-slac-area-map-pdf). Nodes kept verbatim, no simplification.

features.method: Two OpenStreetMap ways named 'PEP Ring Road' (access=private, highway=unclassified), kept as two separate LineStrings because their endpoints do not meet: together they trace only part of the collider ring's circumference, not a closed loop. A ring road is not the buried beam tunnel itself (docs/HEP_ATLAS_GEOMETRY.md Sec1.2); accuracy_m is widened to the ring-road-proxy tier and feature_type is 'beamline' rather than 'ring' because the shape is neither closed nor a claim about the tunnel's exact path.
features.name: PEP-II ring, partially-traced surface access road

provenance.note: OpenStreetMap alone (source type openstreetmap, rank 11) yields at most `approximate` confidence (contract Sec1.2); the shape is also an incomplete, unclosed ring-road proxy for the buried beam tunnel, not the tunnel itself.

map.name: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Menlo Park campus

summary.plain: SLAC's main campus in Menlo Park, California: the 3.2-kilometre linear accelerator (drawn as its above-ground Klystron Gallery), the partially-traced PEP-II collider ring, the BaBar detector's hall, and the hall that hosted the SLD detector and now hosts the DMRadio-m3 axion search.

unlocated.backlog: Find the SLC Design Handbook (SLAC-R-714, December 1984) or a civil-engineering site plan showing the arc paths from the end of the linac to the Collider Experimental Hall; georeference against the linac and hall footprints already drawn.
unlocated.reason: The Stanford Linear Collider's north and south collider arcs and final-focus system, which curve from the end of the linac around to the Collider Experimental Hall, have no OpenStreetMap trace in this session's extract (only named buildings matched; no way named for the arcs or final focus was found) and no fetched source gives their path in coordinates. The interaction point itself is drawn: see geometry:slac-collider-experimental-hall-sld, entity_id site:slac-slc-collider-hall-sld.
